back: The careful management and wise use of resources so they are protected from waste and remain available in future.
Afforestation: planting trees where there was no recent forest. Reforestation: replanting where forest was cut.
Dams, rainwater harvesting, drip irrigation, recycling and reuse, fixing leaks, metering, protecting catchments and wetlands, mulching.
Plantations, controlled cutting by permit, woodlots, alternative fuels, efficient stoves, fire control, laws and education.
Quotas and licences, closed seasons, minimum mesh sizes, restricted breeding areas, banning poison and explosives, fish farming, restocking.
Kapenta introduced from Lake Tanganyika in the 1960s; caught at night from rigs with lights and lift nets; shared by Zimbabwe and Zambia.
Pine, eucalyptus and wattle in the Eastern Highlands (e.g. Nyanga, Chimanimani) supply timber and reduce pressure on natural woodland.

front: Why is falling catch per rig a warning sign?
back: More fishing effort is landing fewer fish, so the stock is being caught faster than it can breed.
